## New: Busch-Jaeger 6257-WL radiator thermostat support

Busch-Jaeger 6257-WL radiator thermostats are now supported through the existing
climate entity, thanks to the included `local-abbfreeathome` 3.13.0 update.
No new integration options are required.

[Integration setup](https://github.com/kingsleyadam/local-abbfreeathome-hass#configuration)

## New: Reauthentication for rejected SysAP credentials

If the System Access Point rejects the stored credentials, for example after a
password change, Home Assistant now asks you to re-authenticate. Enter the new
**Username** and **Password** for the local API; your other integration settings
are kept.

[Local API credentials](https://github.com/kingsleyadam/local-abbfreeathome-hass#local-api-credentials)

## Upcoming: Support for recent Home Assistant versions only

Starting with the release after 1.18.0, this integration will support the
Home Assistant releases from about the last six months: the latest seven monthly
releases (for example 2026.5 to 2026.11), which are the versions it is tested
against. Releases will set a minimum Home Assistant version, and
HACS/Marketplace will not offer an update to a Home Assistant installation
older than that minimum.

The main reason is the growing amount of backwards-compatibility code. Home
Assistant changes its APIs with every release, and supporting older versions
means keeping a separate code path for each change. That code is harder to
maintain and test, and slows down new features.

As Home Assistant publishes new releases, the minimum will move forward, and
code that only supported older versions will be removed. The next release is
expected to require Home Assistant 2026.5 or newer.

If you run an older Home Assistant version, update Home Assistant to keep
receiving integration updates. Integration versions you already have installed
keep working.
